entities.summary:
Fei Yi, courtesy name Wenwei, was a Chinese diplomat, military general, politician, and regent of the state of Shu during the Three Kingdoms period of China. Born in the late Eastern Han dynasty, Fei Yi started his career as an attendant to Liu Shan, the eldest son and heir apparent of Liu Bei, a warlord who became the founding emperor of Shu. After Liu Shan became emperor in 223, Fei Yi gradually rose to prominence under the regency of Zhuge Liang, the Imperial Chancellor of Shu. During this time, Fei Yi played a crucial role in Shu's diplomacy, military campaigns, and administrative reforms. He is also known for his involvement in the famous Battle of Red Cliffs, where he led a contingent of Shu forces against the invading forces of Cao Cao. Fei Yi's leadership and strategic thinking were instrumental in securing Shu's victory and cementing its position as a major power in the Three Kingdoms period. After Zhuge Liang's death in 234, Fei Yi succeeded him as regent and continued to lead Shu's efforts to expand its territory and strengthen its economy. Fei Yi's legacy as a statesman, military leader, and diplomat has endured for centuries, and he remains one of the most celebrated figures of the Three Kingdoms period.

Fei Yi's significance in the Three Kingdoms period cannot be overstated. His leadership and strategic thinking played a crucial role in Shu's military victories, including the Battle of Red Cliffs, and his diplomatic efforts helped to establish Shu as a major power in the region. Fei Yi's legacy has been the subject of numerous historical accounts, including the Records of the Three Kingdoms, which portrays him as a wise and capable leader who was instrumental in shaping Shu's fortunes.

Despite his many accomplishments, Fei Yi's life was marked by tragedy. He died in 253, at the age of 82, leaving behind a legacy that continues to inspire and fascinate historians and scholars today.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fei Yi's leadership and strategic thinking played a crucial role in securing Shu's victory in the Battle of Red Cliffs, one of the most famous battles in Chinese history. His diplomatic efforts helped to establish Shu as a major power in the Three Kingdoms period, and his legacy continues to be celebrated and studied by scholars around the world.
